questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before you turn or change lanes.
Signal continuously. Keep the signal on until your turn or lane change is complete.
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, you don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, you don't need to signal.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before turning or changing lanes. Keep the signal on during the entire turn or lane change. Turn off the signal after you finish your move. Always signal, whether other drivers are near or not.

questions.question: As a truck driver carrying cargo, you are responsible for everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Noticing if the weight is unbalanced.
Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.
questions.explanation: You must check your cargo, notice if weight is unbalanced or overloaded, make sure the cargo is secure, and check that it doesn't block your view or block access to emergency equipment. You are responsible for your cargo even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?
questions.explanation: Getting enough sleep is critical for safe driving. Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, heavy eyelids, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting shoulder rumble strips, or feeling restless and irritable.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving on surfaces with poor traction. Reduce your speed by about one-third when driving on a wet road.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the air storage tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these materials. Tanks with a manual drain valve should be drained at the end of each day.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Make the brakes work without squeaking.
Stop ice from forming in the brake system.
Prevent people from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. This helps prevent ice from forming in the brake system during cold weather.

questions.question: When backing up and the trailer turns, follow it by:

options.text: Not changing anything. The vehicle will naturally follow the trailer.
Changing the direction you turn the steering wheel.
Turning the steering wheel even harder in the direction it is already turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changing the direction you turn the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, start by turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the turn. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the direction of the steering wheel to follow the trailer.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: Cargo loaded with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Increases the chance of a rollover.
Increases the chance that items will fall.
Makes the cargo harder to unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the chance of a rollover.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases the risk that your vehicle will tip over. Always load cargo so the weight is balanced safely.

questions.question: Is texting while driving safer or more dangerous than talking on a cell phone while driving?
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. It distracts your mind and also takes your hands and eyes off the road.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Are not allowed on a vehicle.
Hold compressed air for the brakes.
Should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air that powers the brakes in an air brake system. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and might slow down other drivers, what should you do?

options.text: Drive while using your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive while using your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, turn on your four-way flashers. This warns drivers behind you. (Check your local laws about using flashers.)

questions.question: When you must stop suddenly in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, keep your vehicle going straight. You can still turn if needed, but a straight line stop is safest.

questions.question: When you pull off to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: A driver should keep the driver's side door open.
A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
The driver should wave their arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When you see a law enforcement vehicle on the side of the road with flashing lights, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the side of the road, move to another lane if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a full inspection of your vehicle and explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: After you change a tire, what should you do shortly after?

options.text: Stop to make sure the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to make sure the lug nuts are still tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect the body?

options.text: After several drinks have been consumed.

questions.explanation: Alcohol can affect you after just one drink. It impairs coordination, reaction time, vision, judgment, and decision-making. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out of the vehicle and walks to the back to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out of the vehicle and walks to the back to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when a driver opens the door, leaves their seat, and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During straight line backing, you can only use one look. During other exercises, you can use up to two looks.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are unsure which fire extinguisher to use on a vehicle fire, especially a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them put out the fire.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others
Operating a vehicle that has not been inspected

questions.correctAnswerText: Operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means driving in a selfish, bold, or pushy way. Road rage means operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others or to physically attack another driver or their vehicle.

questions.question: When are you most likely to experience strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it harder to keep your vehicle in its lane. Strong winds are especially a problem when driving out of a tunnel.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before each trip. If you have a trailer, make sure it is straight when you adjust the mirrors.

questions.question: What can water on the road cause?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how should you brake?

options.text: Pump the brakes several times before pressing down hard.
Press the brake pedal as hard as possible every time.

questions.explanation: Drivers with ABS and without ABS should brake the same way. ABS automatically works to prevent wheel lockup when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: What tells you the air pressure in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: A vehicle with air brakes has a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: If a law enforcement vehicle is stopped on the right side of the road with flashing lights, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on a multilane road, move over laws require you to leave the lane next to the vehicle if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more time other vehicles have to move out of the way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: When your brakes fail on a downhill slope, make a decision quickly. The more time you wait, the faster your vehicle will be moving, and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test for a CDL, you may be asked to:
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to check the engine oil level.

questions.question: When taking a driving test for a CDL:

options.text: You must use the same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
You can use any vehicle, even if it is not the type you will drive with the CDL.
The testing station will provide the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the same type of vehicle you will drive with the CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the exact type of vehicle you plan to drive. You must generally provide the vehicle for testing.

questions.question: The two markings on a front brake limiting valve usually say:
questions.explanation: Some older air brake vehicles made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car:

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: If you are convicted of any traffic violation while driving any vehicle, you must notify your employer within 30 days. Parking violations are not included.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Problems with this system are extremely dangerous.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, the examiner will score you on specific driving moves and your overall driving behavior.

questions.question: When making a left turn, you should start the turn:

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
When you reach the center of the intersection or after.
After your rear wheels pass the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you reach the center of the intersection or after.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before you begin turning. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle because of how the truck turns.

questions.question: Rolling backward when you start to accelerate is dangerous because:

options.text: The truck is not designed to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling backward. Rolling backwards may cause you to hit a vehicle or object behind your truck.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer
The maximum weight that a vehicle can tow
The minimum weight that a vehicle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, what is your best way to stop?
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, look for a way to stop outside your vehicle. An escape ramp is the safest way to stop.

questions.question: When can mirror adjustment be checked properly?

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: For vehicles with trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailers are straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.

questions.question: When inspecting your tires, what should you NOT find?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems should not be cut or cracked. All tires on the vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends mainly on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must be:

options.text: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

questions.correctAnswerText: A U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
questions.explanation: You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident to get a hazardous materials endorsement. You will lose this endorsement if you give up your U.S. citizenship.

questions.question: What can overloading a vehicle with cargo do?

options.text: Usually has no effect on the vehicle.
Can affect steering and brake control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect steering and brake control.
questions.explanation: Overloading affects steering, braking, and speed control. Learn to recognize when cargo is too heavy or poorly balanced.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for rear tires?
questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread in every main groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do the same pre-trip inspection before every drive. This routine helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't skip anything.

questions.question: When approaching a bridge or overpass, you should:

options.text: Assume the posted clearance height may not be accurate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the posted clearance height may not be accurate.
questions.explanation: Don't trust posted heights. If the road was repaved or snow is on the ground, the actual opening may be lower than the sign shows. If you're not sure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.
